latest_findings.summary: SkillGen paper explicitly says same held-out instance plus same random seed 42, but observed public ScienceWorld code is an offline fixed-plan benchmark whose eval seed selects instances and whose OpenRouter call exposes no inference seed; model-inference RNG equivalence is therefore not implementation-verified.

The same gap is present in observed public source commit f7304a5595ca35d92500f1be2cceb4aca545fe0b, Git-dated 2026-05-08 before arXiv v1's 2026-05-09 date: llm.py has no exposed inference seed, eval_skill.py samples instances with random.Random(args.seed), and ScienceWorld is already offline-plan. Git time is chronology only.

Historical prepare_scienceworld.py concretely uses seed 42 for deterministic stratified dataset construction, and historical data/scienceworld/test.json identifies itself as scienceworld_test_n100_seed42; this proves an implemented dataset-selection meaning of seed 42 without proving it was the paper's only intended seed semantics.

Targeted indexed searches plus official GitHub tree/releases/actions still did not surface the static ScienceWorld effectiveness baseline/with-skill/summary/skill bundle; negative evidence is limited to checked surfaces.
